relations.subject: Vasudha Dalmia
relations.evidence: Her Ph.D. in German Literature was completed at Jawaharlal Nehru University in South West Delhi in 1984

relations.subject: Vasudha Dalmia
relations.evidence: her Habilitation in Modern Indology and Hindi Literature was completed at the University of Heidelberg in 1995.

relations.subject: Vasudha Dalmia
relations.evidence: From 1974 to 1979, Dalmia had teaching assignments at the University of Tuebingen

relations.subject: Vasudha Dalmia
relations.evidence: she was a research fellow at Jawaharlal University from 1979 to 1984.

relations.subject: Vasudha Dalmia
relations.evidence: She returned to the University of Tuebingen as a lecturer from 1984 until 1997.

relations.subject: Vasudha Dalmia
relations.evidence: Vasudha Dalmia is an Indian professor emerita of Hindi and Modern South Asian Studies in the Department of South and Southeast Asian Studies at the University of California, Berkeley.

relations.subject: Vasudha Dalmia
relations.role: Catherine and William L. Magistretti Distinguished Professorship in South and Southeast Asian Studies
relations.evidence: From 2001 until her retirement in 2012, she was appointed to the Catherine and William L. Magistretti Distinguished Professorship in South and Southeast Asian Studies.

relations.subject: Vasudha Dalmia
relations.object: Free University of Berlin Centre for Interweaving Performance Cultures
relations.evidence: she was a professorial fellow in Fall 2010 at the Free University of Berlin Centre for Interweaving Performance Cultures.

relations.subject: Vasudha Dalmia
relations.role: Chandrika and Ranjan Tandon Professor of Hindu Studies
relations.evidence: From 2013 to 2014, she was the Chandrika and Ranjan Tandon Professor of Hindu Studies at Yale University.

relations.subject: Vasudha Dalmia
relations.evidence: Dalmia co-edited with Heinrich von Stietencron and contributed the essay "Practical Vedanta" to Representing Hinduism
